title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC1RC_0RF1LD_1LE0LB_1LB0RA_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC1RC_0RF1LD_1LE0LB_1LB0RA_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The tape is runs of the word 11110 with travelling defects; the arrangement looks irregular. Lean proves that any halt happens at the right edge of the written tape (state F reading blank tape).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 1 under the head, 0 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 93,732 cells have been visited and 61,827 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.769). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.406).

claims.title: The structure of the run
claims.text: Bouncer growing mostly to the left: the tape is runs of the word 11110 with defects (1110, 1111110) that travel and multiply; one long run of 11110 shrinks by two words per few sweeps. Can halt only at the right edge (Lean).

claims.title: Halting only at the right edge
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of 3 cells covers the whole run from blank tape; in it the halting transition F0 fires only with blank tape from the head onward, and past the head two 0s in a row occur only in the blank region.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No closed rule set has been found; see the README for what a proof would need.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This page runs the machine in your browser and describes the structure seen in its run.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 93,732 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Any halt happens with blank tape from the head on (Lean).

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: The tape reads as runs of the word c = 11110 with defects 1 b (= 1110) and 1 d (= 1111110) between them. The defects travel with the sweeps and change; a long run c28 shrinks by two words every few sweeps. The left end grows fast (bursts of 1 to 7 cells), the right end slowly.

the tape at the left end (b = 110, c = 11110, d = 111110):
step 32,055  E 0 1 b 1 d 1 d c^4 1 b c^4 1 b c^28 1 b c^3 1^3
step 33,737  B 0^2 b c 1 b c^2 1 b c^5 1 b c^4 1 b c^28 1 b c 1^4
step 42,500  B 0^2 b c 1 b c^4 1 d 1 b 1 d 1 d 1 d 1 d 1 d 1 d c^4 1 b c^4 1 b c^26 1^2
step 43,987  D 0 b^2 d c^2 1 b c^3 1 d 1 d 1 b c^2 1 b c^2 1 b c^4 1 d 1 d c^2 1 d 1 d c^24 1^4

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 0. Lean proves (a closed tape language of windows of 3 cells, kernel-checked) that F can read that 0 only with blank tape from the head on: at the right edge.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.769). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.406).
After 109 steps the tape spans 93,732 cells (60,607 left of the start, 9,182 right), with a density of 1s of 0.66.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer growing mostly to the left: the tape is runs of the word 11110 with defects (1110, 1111110) that travel and multiply; one long run of 11110 shrinks by two words per few sweeps. Can halt only at the right edge (Lean).
family: bouncer over 11110 blocks with travelling defects (chaotic)
